device.name: ELK-BLEDOM BLE LED Strip Controller
device.notes:
Generic BLE LED strip controllers sold under dozens of brand names: JACKYLED, auraLED, HueLite, MELK, LEDBLE, ELK-BULB, ELK-LAMPL, and many others. Extremely cheap ($2-15) PWM LED controllers with a common BLE protocol. Advertises HID service 0x1812 but does not actually implement it — ignore.
PROTOCOL: fixed 9-byte packets with envelope [0x7E, seq, cmd, p1, p2, p3, p4, flag, 0xEF]. Byte 2 is a per-command sequence number (0x00 works; app uses unique values). Byte 8 is typically 0x00 or 0x10 but does not affect functionality. No bonding, no auth. NOT write-only: devices send 9-byte 7E…EF state notifications on characteristic 0xFFF4 (power state 0x23/0xF0/0x01 = on, 0x24/0x00 = off, plus RGB and brightness), and a state query command exists (7e 00 01 fa 00 00 00 00 ef).
Commands are grouped: command byte 3 identifies the operation category, byte 4 the sub-command. The app distinguishes "data" vs "control" messages but they use the same packet format.
DISCOVERY: service UUID 0xFFF0 is the reliable signal. Advertised names vary widely: "ELK-BLEDOM", "MELK", "LEDBLE", "ELK-BULB", "ELK-LAMPL". No pairing required — any central in range can connect and write.
UUID FAMILIES: the 0xFFF0/0xFFF3/0xFFF4 set does not cover every advertised name. LEDBLE, JACKYLED, "LED-" and XROCKER variants use write 0xFFE1 / notify 0xFFE2; DMRRBA-007 uses the Nordic UART service (write 0x6E400002, notify 0x6E400003).
OPT7 BRAND VARIANT: OPT7 (motorcycle/automotive accent lighting) ships the same protocol; its Android app is a rebrand of the common "LED lamp" OEM app. Its name matcher accepts additional advertised names: prefixes DCS-O, ELZ-O, CS-FanLED, MHRS-QA and "LED LIGHT STRIP", substring matches "OB", "OE" and "E2P", plus WCT-family names via DeviceName constants (ELK-BTCWCT*/ELK-BLEDWCT* and brand+suffix compositions such as "OPT7" + "-BLED"/"-BLEDWCT").
SECOND CONTROL PATH — connectionless broadcast: besides the GATT connection, the app can control devices purely over BLE advertising — the PHONE itself advertises command frames (its broadcast builders assemble AdvertiseData and call startAdvertising, managed by a broadcast manager). The UUID 90B1F4D2-6C0E-43D6-BA91-A8BBBC9375AA seen in this app is NOT a GATT UUID: it is the fixed address/addressId the app assigns the broadcast pseudo-device in its internal device database.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for service UUID, characteristic UUID, packet format, color/brightness/color-temperature commands — sourced from github.com/FergusInLondon/ELK-BLEDOM, a clean-room RE from the Android APK. State readback (0xFFF4), the MELK/MODELX login handshake, the alternate UUID families and the scheduler/time-sync/mic commands are sourced from github.com/dave-code-ruiz/elkbledom (actively maintained HACS component). Commands beyond the visual ones (timing, mic streaming) are documented but less tested.

credentials.notes: No auth. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state. Power-cycling resets to default state.

steps.expect: Device powers on in default state.

methods.description: Scan for 0xFFF0 service UUID, connect, and write 9-byte packets to characteristic 0xFFF3. Classic devices need no initialization sequence; newer MELK-*/MODELX firmware disconnects unless a login handshake (7e 07 83, then 7e 04 04, about 1 s apart) is written immediately after connect.

steps.action: Scan for the 0xFFF0 service UUID (ignore HID 0x1812) and connect.

setup.notes: No provisioning. Device advertises when powered. No bonding or pairing required and no authentication. Not write-only: state notifications arrive on 0xFFF4 — subscribe to it for feedback.

rejoin.notes: No bonding. Any central within range can connect and write.

variants.notes: OPT7 brand variant (app com.opt7.glow). Its matcher also accepts the advertised-name patterns listed in device.notes (DCS-O, ELZ-O, CS-FanLED, MHRS-QA, "LED LIGHT STRIP", and names containing "OB", "OE" or "E2P", plus WCT-family names). Supports the connectionless advertising-broadcast control path described in device.notes.

entities.name: LED Strip
entities.notes: set_effect is deliberately unbound: set_mode's command byte varies by app version and has no default, so no single effect frame can be built from the spec alone.

get_state.description: Query device state (command 0x01, sub-command 0xFA). The 9-byte state response arrives as a notification on 0xFFF4.

set_brightness.description: Set brightness. Command 0x01. Brightness 0-100 (0x64) at the app level; light_mode 0-255.

set_color_temperature.description: Set color temperature. Command 0x05, sub-command 0x02. warm and cold values must total 100.

set_effect_speed.description: Set effect speed. Command 0x02, speed in byte 3.

set_light_on_off.description: Turn light on or off. Command byte varies by app version. On = 0x01, Off = 0x00.

set_mic_on_off.description: External microphone on/off (command 0x04, sub-command 0x07). On = 0x01, off = 0x00.

set_mode.description: Set effect mode. Index 0-255 per app mode list (strobe, fade, etc.).

set_rgb_color.description: Set RGB color. Command 0x05, sub-command 0x03. Red, green, blue are uint8 values (0-255).

set_scheduler.description: Scheduler on/off. Command 0x82: hours, minutes, then 0x00, 0x00 = schedule on / 0x01 = schedule off, and a days bitmask (add 0x80 when the schedule is enabled).

set_single_color.description: Set a predefined single color. Command 0x05, sub-command 0x01. Color index 0-100 (maps to app's single-color palette).

sync_time.description: Sync the device clock. Command 0x83: hours, minutes, seconds, ISO day-of-week (1-7).

turn_off.description: Power off, as the constant frame the dave-code-ruiz/elkbledom HACS integration writes (see helpful_urls): command 0x04 with payload 00 00 00. Counterpart of turn_on.

turn_on.description: Power on, as the constant frame the dave-code-ruiz/elkbledom HACS integration writes (see helpful_urls): command 0x04 with payload F0 00 01. Unlike set_light_on_off this needs no app-version-dependent command byte, so it is directly bindable.

characteristics.name: Write
characteristics.notes: Write characteristic for all commands. No framing declared because each 9-byte write is a complete packet. State responses and notifications arrive on 0xFFF4.

characteristics.name: Notify
characteristics.notes: State notifications. The device pushes 9-byte 7E…EF packets here — power state (0x23/0xF0/0x01 = on, 0x24/0x00 = off), RGB values and brightness — including the response to the 0xFA state query. Subscribe to it for state readback.

services.name: ELK-BLEDOM Service
services.notes:
Single service with a write characteristic (0xFFF3) and a notify characteristic (0xFFF4) that carries state responses. All packets use the 9-byte format: [0x7E] [seq] [cmd] [p1] [p2] [p3] [p4] [flag] [0xEF].
Byte 2 (sequence) can be 0x00 for basic operation. Byte 8 (flag) is typically 0x00 or 0x10 — both work identically.
